To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the host interferon-stimulate genes (ISGs) are critical for the control of hepatitis C virus ( HCV ) replication and ISGs are emerging as novel targets for antiviral therapy.

(i) HCV infection induces the expression of a wide range of ISGs, which can modulate IFN signaling and IFN-mediated anti-viral actions, and (ii) emerging ISGs identified from genome-wide RNAi screens can modulate HCV replication, and may represent new therapeutic targets for HCV infection.

(1) HCV infection induces the expression of ISGs that modulate the IFN pathway; and (2) the expression of these ISGs is regulated by cellular determinants critical to the innate immune response against HCV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which HCV evades the host innate immune responses and the roles of ISGs in the host defense.
the molecular mechanisms of innate immune responses to HCV infection and the development of new antiviral therapies.
the molecular mechanisms of HCV replication and host innate immune response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ISG system is a complex network of signaling pathways and effector molecules that are critical for host defense against viral pathogens.
the ISGs play a critical role in controlling HCV replication, but the exact mechanism is still unknown.
the innate immune response plays an essential role in controlling HCV infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ISGs are critical regulators of the innate immune response against HCV.
the ISG expression profile can be used as a biomarker to identify patients with a high risk of developing HCV-related liver diseases.
HCV has evolved a variety of strategies to subvert the host innate immunity, which has led to a complex and dynamic interaction between HCV and the innate immune system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ISGs are not only involved in IFN signaling, but also play critical roles in the regulation of the innate immune response, which may be important for the control of viral replication.
HCV infection is a complex process that involves the interplay between the host and virus.
HCV has developed multiple mechanisms to evade host antiviral responses.
